messages:
jess: Ran nsys + nvtx on staging to chase the p95 regressions after the kernel update. Repro: batch=4, seq_len=2048, amp=true, TRT 8.2. Seen a weird host-side stall in the vLLM->TRT wrapper before engine execute.

sam: Can you paste the nsys summary / top-level hotspots?

jess: Quick snippets from the timeline summary: 
```
CUDA memcpy HtoD: 1.2ms (hot loop spikes)
TRT execute: 0.9ms
wrapper host overhead (prepare+submit): 2.8ms
scheduler spin-loop (host poll): 1.6ms
```
nvtx shows memcpy spikes coincident with KV cache misses (first tokens after cache coldstart).

maria: Are we falling back to a scalar / unpacked kernel anywhere? The selector logs changed in the recent PR.

jess: Selector log: "autoselect: fallback kernel=layernorm_fp32_packed->layernorm_fp32_unpacked (reason: dtype mismatch)". That forced a tensor re-layout path and extra memcpy to temporary workspace.

sam: That explains extra HtoD copies and wrapper stalls — layout remap on host before enqueue. Any perfetto slices to inspect?

jess: Uploaded a small perfetto trace (private gist). Repro command I used: 
```
nsys profile --output=/tmp/nsys_run --trace=cuda,cupti python -m tests/perf/run_infer --model gpt-small --batch 4 --max-tokens 2048
```
I also added NVTX markers around: wrapper.prepare, wrapper.enqueue, kvcache.fetch, engine.execute. The timeline clearly shows long gaps between prepare -> enqueue where memcpy happens.

perf-bot: alert: p95 latency = 318ms (baseline 240ms) :rotating_light:

maria: Quick experiment: override kernel table to prefer the "packed" layout kernel for seq_len >= 1024 and same dtype. Jess — can you try patching selector to avoid the fallback path?

jess: Applied a local override and re-ran. Results: p95 dropped to 255ms. memcpy HtoD spikes reduced to ~0.3ms, wrapper overhead ~1.1ms. So the layout fallback was the culprit.

sam: Great catch. We should add a regression test that asserts selector picks packed kernel for long sequences instead of the fallback. Also instrument a metric for kernel_fallback_count.

jess: On it. I'll open a PR with: selector tweak + unit + nvtx annotations in wrapper code + a small perf test to catch this class of regressions.

infra-bot: deploy-preview jess/selector-fix built: https://ci.internal/1234 :rocket:

maria: Another follow-up: batching heuristics currently try to merge short requests which may flip layout assumptions. We should ensure autoscaler/batcher doesn't create micro-batches that trigger fallback kernels.

sam: Agreed — add a rule: for models with layout-sensitive kernels prefer batch packing that preserves contiguous layout or prefer per-request padding instead of re-layout.

jess: Filed task RT-4321 "kernel selector: avoid layout fallback for large seqs + batching heuristics".

maria: Also add tracing for kv cache coldstart count so we can correlate with memcpy spikes.

jess: Will add telemetry + a Grafana panel for kernel_fallback_count vs p95. Thanks all :thumbsup:
